Lessons.Title: Changes over Equal Intervals
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: compare output changes over equal input intervals for linear and exponential functions, recognize interval-length dependence and explain how an exponential factor over k steps equals b^k. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 5 Lesson 20, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/5/20/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/5/20/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source compares graph segments and tables with equal widths.

Original functions over nonnegative whole t: L(t)=4+3t and E(t)=4(1.5)^t. On a two-step interval [t,t+2], L gains6 units for every t, since 3×2=6. E's output is multiplied by (1.5)^2=2.25 for every starting t, so E(t+2)/E(t)=2.25 despite the absolute change varying.

Compute L0=4,L2=10,L4=16; each two-step difference6. E0=4,E2=9,E4=20.25; successive ratios9/4=2.25,20.25/9=2.25, but additive gains5 and11.25 differ. An analysis that compares E0→E2 with L2→L4 still uses equal duration but changes baselines; state the interval explicitly.

Student task: calculate repeated equal-width intervals for both models, identify preserved quantity (difference versus ratio), and generalize a k-step relation. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for interval math, correct invariant, algebraic generalization and clear interpretation of graph segment comparisons.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equal-width linear changes
KeyConcepts.Definition: The increment over k steps is mk for f(t)=mt+b.
KeyConcepts.Example: L gains3×2=6 in any two-step interval.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equal-width exponential factor
KeyConcepts.Definition: For f(t)=ab^t, ratio f(t+k)/f(t)=b^k when outputs nonzero.
KeyConcepts.Example: E multiplies by1.5²=2.25 per two steps.

KeyConcepts.Title: Absolute versus relative difference
KeyConcepts.Definition: Exponential equal-period ratios are fixed while absolute gains vary.
KeyConcepts.Example: E gains5 then11.25 over consecutive two-step intervals.

WorkedExamples.Question: Evaluate L0,L2,L4.

WorkedExamples.Title: Generalize k-step relation
WorkedExamples.Question: Show E(t+k)/E(t) for E(t)=4×1.5^t.
WorkedExamples.Method: Work from the explicitly fictional data and verify the original model, units and domain.
Steps: Use exponent sum identity to factor1.5^t×1.5^k.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming exponential equal-period differences are fixed
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It is ratios that stay constant.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Forgetting interval length in exponential factor
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Over two steps factor is b², not b.

SummaryPoints: Equal input intervals reveal constant differences for linear functions and constant ratios for exponentials.
L gains6 over every two steps; E multiplies2.25.
Exponential absolute gains can grow even with constant relative multiplier.
